rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course and generate measurements. Geometry: five sensors spread across x = -0.04 to +0.04 m at y = 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the line is seen by several sensors at once on bends. Sensor size 0.012 m is a middle value that covers the 25 mm tape without washing out the signal. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority, and mass 0.8 kg with a 0.12 m body width keeps the off-track margin reasonable. Controller: symmetric weights [-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5] make the signal sign follow the tape side (positive = left). base_speed 1.6 gives about 80 percent of full PWM, which should reach the roughly 1.5 m/s needed for the 3 s limit without being so fast that the robot leaves the line. kp 3.0 gives a strong steering response (about 1050 PWM per unit signal). kd 0.3 damps oscillation and ki 0.02 is small to avoid integral windup. line_loss 'last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the tape. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with the slalom possibly showing oscillation or some line loss. Hypotheses to test: (1) if steering_oscillation is high, kp is too large or kd too small; (2) if max_error approaches the off-track limit on sharp bends, base_speed is too high; (3) if completion_time is above 3 s, base_speed needs to go up. Next measurements: rms_error, max_error, completion_time, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each development track.
